title: Spindle: Efficient Distributed Training of Multi-Task Large Models via Wavefront Scheduling
problem: Training multi-task, multi-modal (MT MM) foundation models is inefficient because their heterogeneous model components and diverse workloads across tasks and modalities create complex dependency patterns that existing parallelism strategies cannot jointly optimize. No existing distributed training system addresses the combined challenges of workload heterogeneity and dependency-driven execution scheduling for MT MM models.
motivation: Foundation models increasingly unify multiple tasks and modalities (e.g., vision-language) under a shared base with specialized components, but the resulting architectural heterogeneity causes severe resource under-utilization in standard data/pipeline/tensor-parallel training systems.
method: Spindle decomposes MT MM model execution into 'waves'—groups of heterogeneous micro-tasks—and applies a two-phase joint optimization: (1) heterogeneity-aware workload parallelization that assigns tasks to devices accounting for differing compute demands per modality, and (2) dependency-driven wavefront scheduling that pipelines waves based on their inter-task data dependencies. The wavefront schedule coordinates execution so that waves from different tasks and modalities overlap in time, filling pipeline bubbles caused by load imbalance.
key_novelty: The wavefront scheduling abstraction that decomposes MT MM model execution into heterogeneous waves and jointly optimizes parallelization and dependency-driven scheduling in a single framework.
contributions: Wavefront scheduling formulation that decomposes MT MM model execution into heterogeneity-aware waves
Heterogeneity-aware workload parallelization strategy for tasks with differing compute demands
Dependency-driven execution scheduling that overlaps waves across tasks and modalities
Up to 71% speedup over state-of-the-art distributed training systems on various MT MM models

metrics.speedup: up to 71% over state-of-the-art training systems

baselines: state-of-the-art distributed training systems (unspecified, likely Megatron-LM / DeepSpeed variants)
limitations: Baseline systems compared against are not explicitly named in the abstract; evaluation scope and MT MM model diversity not fully characterized.
